findings.claim: TestBreachStopAlertsReadTheLedgerOnlyWhileOneIsOpen/ledger-error does not pin that nothing from a failed ledger read is used: the double returns an empty projection with its error and the only seeded stop is an unknown id, so ignoring the error survives (mutation m6 passed).
findings.evidence: go test -overlay with 'projection, _ := read()' in resolveEndedBreachStops: all subtests pass. Production goal.Project and defaultSeatDependencies().Project return Projection{} (nil Tree) on error, so production would resolve nothing either way.
findings.change: Optional: in the ledger-error case, return a tree in which the seeded goal is done together with the error, and keep asserting the episode is unchanged.

findings.claim: A pruned done goal is no longer in the ledger, so its retained breach-stop alert stays open for good under the brief's table.
findings.evidence: goal prune (internal/goal/verbs.go:4339-4349) deletes archived goals outside the retention closure; breachStopEnded returns "" for an id not in the ledger, as the brief's table decides.
findings.change: None for this unit; add to the later list if the live count after U1b lands short.
findings.relation: brief decision: 'A fenced claim, or not in the ledger -> stays open'

findings.claim: While any leftover stands (three fenced claims on the lane), every full pass runs a second ledger projection under the exclusive alerts lock.
findings.evidence: resolveEndedBreachStops calls read() after lockAlerts(lock.Exclusive); openBreachStop stays true for fenced claims until they resume.
findings.change: None; the brief accepts the cost. Watch alert list / alert seen latency on the lane.
findings.relation: brief simplification: one lock, no pre-read under the shared lock

findings.claim: The fail-closed stderr line repeats on every full pass while the ledger is unreadable and a leftover is open.
findings.evidence: tick.go writes 'old budget-stop alerts not ended: ...' to os.Stderr on each resolveEndedBreachStops error.
findings.change: None; the brief specifies the line and it goes to the tick's stderr, not a person's channel.
findings.relation: brief D1: 'A read error writes one stderr line'
